summary: From about 11:00-11:05Z on 2026-11-11 fivo-worker's calls to groq-llm began timing out (30 s) or returning 503, with no deploy or config change on our side. categorize_transaction now takes 12-30 s per attempt, while POST /transactions/quick-add waits a fixed 8,000 ms for the worker result, so nearly every quick-add returns 504 from the 11:05 bucket. Other routes do not wait on the worker and stay healthy. Whether Groq itself or the worker's network path is at fault is not established.

root_cause.component: fivo-worker categorize_transaction -> Groq chat completions call (30 s timeouts and 503s) against quick-add's fixed 8 s result wait
root_cause.summary: Groq calls from fivo-worker degraded at about 11:00-11:05Z (client p95 ~480 ms to ~29 s, error rate 0 to ~0.62). categorize_transaction blocks on these calls, so the worker result arrives long after quick-add's 8 s wait ends, producing 504s. The queue also backs up (depth 0 to 30). The cause of the Groq degradation is not established.

hypotheses.statement: fivo-worker's categorize_transaction fails or retries against groq-llm (timeouts, 503s), stalling the worker so quick-add's 8 s wait for the result expires and returns 504.

supporting.statement: Groq client p95 went from ~480 ms to ~29 s and error rate from 0 to ~0.62, with a level shift at 11:00Z.
Worker-to-Groq spans took 175-589 ms until 11:02 and 11.6-19.9 s from 11:05:10.
All 103 worker warnings in 11:00-11:40Z are categorize_transaction retries mentioning groq: 72 timeouts and 31 503s. The only errors are Groq timeouts.
In the traced failing quick-add the API waited 8,000 ms and gave up; the worker task took 13,033 ms, of which 13,019 ms was the Groq POST.
Worker task p95 pinned at 30,000 ms from 11:05 and queue depth rose from 0 to 30.
No deploys or config changes in the window, consistent with an external trigger.

contradicting.statement: Trace status shows ok for slow Groq calls, so traces are not a usable error signal.
Only 2 warnings mention 429; they were not read, so rate limiting is not excluded as a sub-cause.
Baseline task p95 was ~6 s while Groq p95 was ~480 ms, which is unexplained; the 8 s budget was already tight.

hypotheses.statement: The Celery queue on upstash-redis is stalled (quota, connection limit, broker problem).

supporting.statement: quick-add depends on the Redis queue round trip and no local changes were recorded.

contradicting.statement: 0 worker log lines mention redis; tasks are being received from the queue.
Enqueue took 1.8 ms in the traced request.
quick-add 504 lines show only the 8000 ms result-not-ready error, with no Redis errors.

hypotheses.statement: fivo-worker is saturated by a local long-running job or memory pressure on its 512 MB, two-thread instance.

supporting.statement: The worker has only two threads and beat runs in the same process.

contradicting.statement: Memory flat at 248-256 MB, CPU fell after 11:00, 0 restarts.
embed_pending_receipts finished in 2.62 s and only categorize_transaction produced warnings or errors.
No receipt backlog: only 2 pending receipts.

hypotheses.statement: neon-postgres lock, slow query or data condition on the quick-add write path.

supporting.statement: Nothing of ours changed and only one route is affected, which would also fit a path-specific DB issue.

contradicting.statement: DB spans in the failing trace took 5.8 ms (insert) and 6.0 ms (select).
Writes to transactions continued at normal rates and job failures are Groq timeouts, not DB errors.

facts.statement: quick-add returned 201 through the 11:00 bucket and 504 on every call from the 11:05 bucket; other routes showed no 5xx (counts partial).
Groq client p95 was ~480 ms and error rate 0 at 10:50-10:55; from 11:00 p95 was ~29 s and error rate ~0.62 through 11:35.
All 103 worker warnings in 11:00-11:40Z were categorize_transaction retries on Groq (72 timed out, 31 503); the first sampled warning is at 11:05:09Z.
Trace 654ee93acd37dccd (11:05:51Z): enqueue 1.8 ms, DB insert 5.8 ms, API waited 8,000 ms and errored, worker task took 13,033 ms with the Groq POST 13,019 ms.
Worker queue depth went from 0 to 5 at 11:05 and to 30 at 11:35; task p95 was 30,000 ms from 11:05.
No deploys or config changes for any service 06:00-11:40Z, and none for fivo-worker since 11-09.
quick-add waits on the worker's result via the Redis queue; the worker runs Celery with two threads.
Worker memory, CPU and restarts show no resource exhaustion.

assumptions: Worker thread starvation is inferred from queue depth and task duration, not measured directly; a single slow Groq call already exceeds the 8 s wait.
Queue wait of about 5 s is approximated from span timestamps.
Onset is stated as ~11:00-11:05Z; fast spans at 11:02:50 suggest the true start is closer to 11:03-11:05.
Whether the Groq degradation is provider-side or on the worker's network path is not established; the Groq metrics are our own client-side view.
Only one full trace was examined.

recommended_actions.action: Check Groq's status page and the worker host's network path to api.groq.com now, and confirm the key and account are not rate-limited or over quota.
recommended_actions.rationale: Groq calls from the worker are the failing step; the provider-side versus path question is open.

recommended_actions.action: Mitigate quick-add: return 201 with categorisation deferred (async), or fail over to another categoriser, while Groq is degraded.
recommended_actions.rationale: quick-add's fixed 8 s wait is exceeded by every Groq call at 12-30 s, so every call returns 504.

recommended_actions.action: Lower the Groq client timeout from 30 s and cap retries so a slow upstream cannot hold both worker threads; consider a separate queue or more concurrency for categorize_transaction (watch the broker connection limit from INC-2026-021).
recommended_actions.rationale: 30 s timeouts pin task p95 at 30 s and the queue depth grew to 30.

recommended_actions.action: Read the 2 '429' warnings and check the other worker external dependencies (anthropic, voyage, r2) for the same 11:00 shift.
recommended_actions.rationale: Distinguishes a Groq rate limit or a worker network problem from a provider outage.

recommended_actions.action: Add alerts on groq-llm client p95 and error rate, on worker queue_depth, and on the quick-add 504 rate. Investigate why baseline task p95 was ~6 s against an 8 s wait.
recommended_actions.rationale: The step change at 11:00 was only caught at 11:20 via fivo-api p95, and the 8 s budget was already tight.

missing_evidence: Groq provider status or incident signal and the worker's other external dependencies (S13 was skipped).
Direct measurement of worker thread occupancy.
Upstash metrics were never queried (S7 skipped); pg_stat_activity and lock views were unavailable.
Several log, trace and count results were partial or capped, so counts are lower bounds; only one full trace was examined.
Changes to third-party dependencies and changes before 06:00Z on 11-11 were not checked.

what_changed.what_changed: Groq responses to fivo-worker's categorize_transaction calls began timing out or returning 503 at about 11:00Z. This is upstream behaviour, since nothing of ours was deployed or reconfigured.

before.statement: Groq client p95 was ~480 ms with 0 error rate at 10:50-10:55. Worker-to-Groq spans took 175-589 ms through 11:02. quick-add returned 201, including a 1.15 s success at 11:02:49.

after.statement: From 11:00, Groq client p95 was ~29 s and the error rate ~0.62. Spans from 11:05:10 took 11.6-19.9 s. Worker task p95 sat at 30 s from 11:05. quick-add returned 504 from the 11:05 bucket.
